655.saw: Typed German telegram headers 'Berlin ... Deutsche Gesandtschaft abtlg zwei Stockholm' followed by lowercase pronounceable ten-letter code words (0419: 'umsebosul lanihunci urfiohuso pekayupari / avewuoduxu wadariboau vofucfevel lanofiheta', 8 words, telegram w759/2 no. 4; 0420: w648, 5 lines of 4 words, no. 5). Roll 122 0158: w894 22/7 in capitals 'OZUXOWUDA UKASEETITU ...', 3 lines, 12 words. Roll 108 0516: Christiania tel. 1215 of 1 Oct 1918 giving telegrams 4 and 5 again, in 5-letter groups split from the 10-letter words ('umzeb ozul lanih unci ...'), typed, no decipherment on any of them.
655.note: All named frames match the entry.

656.saw: 1264: w791 GrHQu -> 'Deutscher Mil Att Stockholm', 'Sehr dringend', 5 Teile of 29/30/38/31/33 groups, about 150 five-digit groups, typed, signed Ludendorff, no decipherment. 1257: w769 'legation allemande sthlm', 'funfacht vanadopote' then 5-digit groups (about 40). 1260: w592/26 Deutsches Generalkonsulat Stockholm, about 25 five-digit groups. Roll 122 0156: W628 Legation Allmande Stockholm, 5-digit groups (about 50), typed, no decipherment.

657.saw: Typed four-figure code groups, 13 per row: 0785 is sheet 1 (about 27 rows, with pencil underlinings and marginal annotations), 0786 sheet 2 (about 21 rows, stamped Department of State Jan 11 1917 Approved, Lansing). Pure numeric groups, no decipherment written on them.

658.saw: 0048: pasted-up typed copies of German Lima telegrams of June 1917 ('Fourth/Fifth/Sixth, dated June eighth, German Minister Lima to the German Minister Santiago / Buenos Aires / Consul Quito'), 1-5 digit numbers (about 130 groups), signed Handley, no decipherment. 0104: telegram Lima 24 July 1917 file 862.20223/26 with a letter-code Quito-Lima text ('dobombobet fesafbefys catuhlobaz ...') and four numeric telegrams (17106 3819 14014 ...). 0101: London's reply 'Second undecipherable / Fourth undecipherable' (clear).
658.note: Frame numbers in the entry match; the frames are on medialz M336-064.

849.frame: Newberry Case MS 5017, nby_dig/2714 (case_ms_5017_020_o2), one page
849.saw: English 17th-c. hand: 'Ex eodem lib. Mst. This Table which standeth here underneth serveth them who are desirous to use a form of Characters ...'; a 3x3 grid of cells each giving three letters paired with dotted/stroked marks (a.k.t, b.l.u, c.m.i, d.n.x, e.o.y, f.p.z, g.q, s.r.&, s.w ...), and below it two lines of cipher characters (block/angle strokes with dots) separated by a semicolon, matching the two sample lines. Page carries its own key; no plaintext written beneath the samples.
